WITH SEIZURES\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 43 year old male was brought to the casualty with comlains of involuntary movements of body since today morning.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/b\u003E:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe Patient was apparently asymptomatic 4 days back when he had a binge of alcohol . he lost consciousness at his workplace and was taken to the hospital. At the hospital, the correction fluids were given and the patient was sent home. Today morning he had 2 episodes of involuntary movement of body (tonic movements with stiffening of body) lasting 1-2 minutes and relieved on itself.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHis wife checked his grbs at home after this episode and it was found to be 60mg\/dl after which he was rushed to the hospital. In the hospital the correction was done inspite of which involuntary movements continued. He was then brought to our hospital.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo uprolling of eyes or loss of consciousness during the episodes.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo c\/o vomitings, headache, frothing from mouth, deviation of mouth, tongue bite, post ictal confusion, involuntary micturition\/defecation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ciframe allowfullscreen='allowfullscreen' webkitallowfullscreen='webkitallowfullscreen' mozallowfullscreen='mozallowfullscreen' width='320' height='266' src='https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/video.g?token=AD6v5dz2uZ5vWHoUYbrLRLmSzVRzJ7I6Mu2Yys8ihsu39qOkyV658kfhxJ94mEGjMmRiVAvkokvidltuINHUwfBkLg' class='b-hbp-video b-uploaded' frameborder='0'\u003E\u003C\/iframe\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/b\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo similar complains in the past.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EK\/C\/O DM-II since 5 years on insulin. He was diagnosed with DM-II Incidently during an episode of fever for which he was initially prescribed OHA'S. The patient used to skip taking his medication. Due non compliance and very high sugars he was then shifted to insulin.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EN\/k\/c\/o HTN, CVA, CAD, Bronchial asthma, thyroid disorders.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDAILY ROUTINE :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient works as an attender in a college.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe lives with his wife and three children.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe doesn't always follow his routine and go to the college.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe gets up in the morning and freshens up and has breakfast. After his family leaves for work\/college, he either goes to college or goes out with his friends and drinks alcohol.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe often skips meals\u0026nbsp; as he forgets about them while he is drinking alcohol. He often consumes food late at night when he is very hungry.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe alcohol consumption has increased in the last 1 year.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn enquiring about the reason of chronic alcoholism with his family, they say that they can't think of any triggers as such.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiet: mixed\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAppetite: lost\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESleep: adequate\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBowel: regular\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMicturition: normal\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAddictions: drinks alcohol since 20 years, chews gutka since 1 year\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAllergies: nil\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFamily history\u003C\/b\u003E: not significant\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EGENERAL EXAMINATION\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient is examined in a well lit room after taking an informed consent.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient is conscious and coherent.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo signs of pallor, icterus, clubbing, cyanosis, generalized lymphadenopathy, pedal edema\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
